title: Apple’s M6 iMac is here: What’s new and which model to buy
content:
Macworld





Apple has updated the iMac with its M6 chip, bringing faster processing, stronger graphics, and improved AI capabilities to its colorful all-in-one desktop. Announced on October 27, 2026, the new model replaces the M4 iMac introduced in 2024, with Apple skipping the M5 generation.
The five biggest upgrades are faster CPU performance, more powerful graphics, improved AI processing, faster SSD storage, and upgraded networking. Both configurations gain additional CPU and GPU cores, a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, and greater memory bandwidth.
Connectivity improves with Wi-Fi 7, Bluetooth 6, and available 2.5Gb Ethernet. However, the familiar 24-inch design remains, along with the seven color options, 4.5K Retina display, and 12MP Center Stage camera. Starting memory and storage are unchanged at 16GB and 256GB.
The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port model and $1,699 for the four-port version. Preorders open October 28, with deliveries and store availability beginning November 6.
M6 vs. M4 iMac: The biggest changes
The upgrades differ slightly depending on whether you choose the two-port or four-port model.


FeatureM6 four-portM6 two-portM4 four-portM4 two-port

CPU12 cores10 cores10 cores8 cores
CPU architecture2 super + 4 performance + 6 efficiency cores2 super + 3 performance + 5 efficiency cores4 performance + 6 efficiency cores4 performance + 4 efficiency cores
GPU12 cores10 cores10 cores8 cores
GPU Neural AcceleratorsAddedAddedNo dedicated accelerator in each GPU coreNo dedicated accelerator in each GPU core
Neural EngineDual 16-coreDual 16-core16-core16-core
Memory bandwidthUp to 170GB/sUp to 170GB/s120GB/s120GB/s
SSD performanceUp to 2× faster, Apple claims*Up to 2× faster, Apple claims*Previous-generation storagePrevious-generation storage
Wi-FiWi-Fi 7Wi-Fi 7Wi-Fi 6EWi-Fi 6E
BluetoothBluetooth 6Bluetooth 6Bluetooth 5.3Bluetooth 5.3
Ethernet2.5Gb includedOptional 2.5GbGigabit includedOptional Gigabit

 Apple’s SSD claim is based on specified test configurations.






M6 iMac release date: When will it launch?
Preorders: October 28, 2026
On sale: November 6
Apple announced the M6 iMac on October 27, 2026. Preorders open on Wednesday, October 28, at:
10:10 a.m. Pacific
1:10 p.m. Eastern
5:10 p.m. GMT
The new iMac will begin arriving with customers on Friday, November 6, when it also becomes available in Apple Stores and through Apple Authorized Resellers. Customers can preorder through Apple’s website or the Apple Store app.
Preorder an M6 iMac from Apple U.S.
Preorder an M6 iMac from Apple U.K.


							


M6 iMac design: What has changed?

				
					

				
			There are still seven different colors available for iMac.
Apple




The M6 iMac retains the slim, colorful design introduced with the M1 model in 2021. It has white display bezels, a colored chin beneath the screen, and a matching stand. There is no notch.
Apple continues to offer seven finishes: blue, green, pink, orange, yellow, purple, and silver. Despite pre-launch speculation about new colors, Apple has not announced any new color options.


						

							




Dimensions and weights are unchanged from the equivalent M4 models:


MeasurementTwo-port M6 iMacFour-port M6 iMac
Height46.1cm / 18.1 inches46.1cm / 18.1 inches
Width54.7cm / 21.5 inches54.7cm / 21.5 inches
Depth, including stand14.7cm / 5.8 inches14.7cm / 5.8 inches
Weight4.42kg4.44kg

 






Keyboard and mouse

				
					

				
			Why stop at matching keyboard and mouse when you can also match your HomePods?
Apple




Both models retain color-matched Magic accessories. The two-port model includes a Magic Keyboard with a Lock key. Buyers can configure it with a Magic Keyboard featuring Touch ID and a numeric keypad. The four-port model includes a Touch ID keyboard, with a numeric-keypad version available as an option.




Both configurations offer a Magic Mouse or an optional Magic Trackpad. USB-C charging for these accessories carries over from the M4 generation.


						

							




M6 iMac display: Is the screen better?

				
					

				
			New iMac, same screen

Apple




The display specifications are unchanged. Both models have a 24-inch LED-backlit 4.5K Retina display, with an actual diagonal measurement of 23.5 inches.


Display specificationM6 iMac & M4 iMac

Resolution4480 × 2520 pixels
Pixel density218ppi
Brightness500 nits
ColorP3 wide color; support for 1 billion colors
True ToneYes
Nano-texture glassOptional on the four-port model

 



Nano-texture glass remains an option for reducing reflections in bright environments.
The camera and audio specifications also carry over: a 12MP Center Stage camera with Desk View and 1080p video recording, a six-speaker system with force-cancelling woofers, Dolby Atmos Spatial Audio, and a three-microphone array.


M6 iMac processor: How much faster is it?

				
					

				
			The M6 is now in the iMac

Apple




The M6 is manufactured using a 2-nanometer process, replacing the second-generation 3nm technology used for M4. The smaller process increases transistor density and helps improve performance and power efficiency.
CPU and graphics
The two-port iMac moves from an eight-core CPU and GPU to ten cores of each. That is a 25 percent increase in core counts.
The four-port model moves from a ten-core CPU and GPU to twelve cores of each—a 20 percent increase. That’s more cores, not necessarily a measured speed improvements.
Both M6 configurations introduce two super cores. The entry model pairs these with three performance cores and five efficiency cores; the four-port version has four performance cores and six efficiency cores.
Neural Engine and AI processing
Both configurations gain a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, replacing M4’s single 16-core engine. Neural Accelerators in the GPU add further processing capability for supported AI workloads.
Memory bandwidth for both M6 models increases from 120GB/s to as much as 170GB/s—approximately 42 percent higher.


						

							




Apple’s performance claims
Apple reports the following improvements over M4 in its specified tests:


WorkloadClaimed improvement

Productivity tasks, including ExcelUp to 1.5×
Graphics tasks, including Affinity photo editingUp to 2×
Ray-traced gamingUp to 2×
Local AI prompt processing in LM StudioUp to 5×
Neural Engine AI computeUp to 2×

 



Apple identifies a 10-core M4 with 32GB memory and a 2TB SSD as its previous-generation comparison configuration.
Media engine
Apple lists the same media-format capabilities across both generations: hardware acceleration for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, plus AV1 decoding.
M6 iMac RAM: How much memory does it have?
Memory capacities are unchanged:


ModelStandard memoryAvailable upgrades

Two-port M6 iMac16GB24GB
Four-port M6 iMac16GB24GB or 32GB

 



The main change is faster access to memory, rather than more included RAM.
For everyday browsing, office applications, and family use, 16GB should be sufficient. Buyers working with larger creative projects or demanding multitasking should consider 24GB. The four-port model’s 32GB option offers more headroom for memory-intensive applications and larger local AI models.
Unified memory is shared by the CPU, GPU, and other components. More capacity lets applications and local models hold more data in memory, potentially reducing reliance on SSD swap.


M6 iMac connectivity: What’s new?

				
					

				
			
Apple




Both models upgrade from Wi-Fi 6E to Wi-Fi 7 and from Bluetooth 5.3 to Bluetooth 6.
Ethernet improves too. Apple’s comparison documents list optional 2.5Gb Ethernet on the two-port M6 model and include it as standard on the four-port version. Their M4 equivalents offered optional and standard Gigabit Ethernet, respectively.
The higher Ethernet connection speed can benefit transfers to compatible network storage, but requires suitable network equipment.
Apple also lists its N1 wireless networking chip and Thread support. 
Port counts remain unchanged: two Thunderbolt/USB 4 ports on the entry model and four Thunderbolt 4 ports on the higher version. The 3.5mm headphone socket retains support for high-impedance headphones.
The color-matched magnetic 143W power adapter connector remains.


						

							




M6 iMac price: How much will it cost?
The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 for the two-port model and $1,699 for the four-port model, both with 16GB memory and a 256GB SSD.
Those prices match the outgoing M4 prices, but they are $200 higher than the M4’s original 2024 launch prices, which Apple increased in June 2026.


ConfigurationM6 starting priceM4 price after June 2026 increaseM4 original launch price

Two-port, 16GB/256GB$1,499/£1,499$1,499/£1,499$1,299/£1,299
Four-port, 16GB/256GB$1,699/£1,699$1,699/£1,699$1,499/£1,499

 




The entry-level storage remains 256GB. The two-port model can be configured with 512GB or 1TB; the four-port model adds a 2TB option. These capacities match the M4 iMac.


Should you buy the M6 iMac?
The M6 iMac is the most compelling for buyers replacing an older Intel iMac or seeking an integrated desktop with a display, camera, speakers, keyboard, and mouse.
M4 owners have less reason to upgrade unless a particular workload is already limiting them. The screen, camera, audio hardware, memory capacities, and overall design remain familiar. Independent testing will establish how much difference M6 makes in everyday use.
Which model should you buy?
Choose the two-port model for everyday home computing, schoolwork, browsing, and office applications. It receives the headline Neural Engine and memory-bandwidth improvements, so buyers do not need the four-port model simply to obtain those upgrades.
Choose the four-port model for its faster 12-core CPU and GPU, additional connections, included Ethernet, and Touch ID keyboard. It also supports 32GB memory and 2TB storage configurations.
For a flexible home-office or creative setup, our provisional recommendation is the four-port model with 24GB memory and a 512GB SSD, subject to upgrade pricing. Buyers running larger local AI models should assess whether the 32GB option meets their software’s requirements.
A substantially discounted M4 remains worth considering for everyday use. Compare equivalent memory, storage, and port configurations when judging the saving.

title: M5 vs. M6 MacBook Pro Buyer's Guide: All Differences Compared
content:
Apple today replaced the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro with a new M6 model, bringing more CPU and GPU cores, upgraded wireless connectivity, and more. How much has changed, and is it worth upgrading or choosing the newer model?



The M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌ retains the previous model's design and most of its specifications, concentrating its improvements on processing performance and connectivity. Both models offer 16GB of starting memory, 1TB of starting storage, and up to 24 hours of battery life.

removed that configuration in March, making 1TB standard and increasing the starting price to $1,699. A further price increase in June brought it to $1,999 amid rising memory and storage costs. The M6 replaces that model at the same price.

Here are all of the differences between the entry-level M5 and M6 ‌MacBook Pro‌ models:







14-Inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ (M5, 2025)
14-Inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ (M6, 2026)


M5 chip made with TSMC's third-generation 3nm process (N3P)
M6 chip made with TSMC's first-generation 2nm process (N2)


FinFET transistors
Gate-all-around nanosheet transistors


10-core CPU
12-core CPU


4 super cores and 6 efficiency cores
2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores


10-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in every core
12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator in every core


Enhanced shader cores
Updated shader core architecture


Second-generation Dynamic Caching
Third-generation Dynamic Caching


16-core Neural Engine
Dual 16-core Neural Engine, totaling 32 cores


153GB/s memory bandwidth across all memory configurations
16GB memory: 153GB/s
24GB or 32GB memory: 170GB/s


Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax)
Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be)


Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 6


Broadcom wireless networking chip
Apple N1 wireless networking chip



Thread networking support


Supports two external 4K displays at up to 144Hz each
Supports two external 4K displays at up to 165Hz each


Originally offered with 512GB storage; started with 1TB from March 2026
Starts with 1TB storage


Originally $1,599; $1,699 from March and $1,999 from June; now discontinued by Apple
Starts at $1,999




Should You Upgrade From the M5 MacBook Pro?

For existing M5 ‌MacBook Pro‌ owners, there is very little reason to upgrade. The M6 is a small refresh aimed primarily at buyers replacing a much older machine, with improvements to performance and connectivity that leave the overall experience essentially unchanged. It offers no increase in memory capacity, additional ports, or longer battery life. If the M5 model already handles your work comfortably, the newer model provides little practical incentive to replace it.

reportedly planned for as early as the first half of 2027, potentially offering a more substantial upgrade than the M6 refresh.

Should You Buy the M5 or M6 MacBook Pro?

For buyers replacing an Intel-based Mac or an older Apple silicon machine, the M5 and M6 deliver much the same experience. The more consequential improvements come from the hardware they share, so the price and configuration should carry more weight than the chip generation.


 
M5 vs. M6 Chip Buyer's Guide: How Much Better Really Is M6?



At the same price, memory, storage, and condition, choose the M6. Its newer chip and wireless connectivity are welcome additions, but there is little reason to pay substantially more for them. A discounted M5 model is likely to be the better value for many buyers.

discontinued in March. If you do not need 1TB of internal storage, this version may provide a more affordable route to essentially the same ‌MacBook Pro‌ experience. The M6 starts at 1TB, leaving no equivalent lower-capacity option.

title: M4 vs. M6 iMac Buyer's Guide: Should You Upgrade?
content:
Apple's latest iMac skips the M5 chip and moves directly to the M6, bringing faster performance, improved connectivity, and faster storage. So how much has changed since the M4 model arrived in 2024, and is it worth upgrading?


The M6 iMac starts at $1,499 in the United States, with the four-port configuration starting at $1,699. While the entry price is $200 higher than the M4 model's original $1,299 launch price, the outgoing model had already risen to $1,499 earlier in 2026.

With much of the ‌iMac‌ experience unchanged, existing M4 owners may be weighing up whether the performance improvements justify replacing their machine, while new buyers may be considering a discounted older model. Here are the key differences between the M4 and M6 ‌iMac‌:



‌iMac‌ (M4, 2024)
‌iMac‌ (M6, 2026)


M4 chip made using TSMC's second-generation 3nm process (N3E)
M6 chip made using TSMC's first-generation 2nm process (N2)


FinFET transistors
Gate-all-around nanosheet transistors


Two-port model: 8-core CPU with 4 performance cores and 4 efficiency cores
Four-port model: 10-core CPU with 4 performance cores and 6 efficiency cores
Two-port model: 10-core CPU with 2 super cores, 3 performance cores, and 5 efficiency cores
Four-port model: 12-core CPU with 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores


Two CPU core types: performance and efficiency
Three CPU core types: super, performance, and efficiency


Two-port model: 8-core GPU
Four-port model: 10-core GPU
Two-port model: 10-core GPU
Four-port model: 12-core GPU



Integrated Neural Accelerator in every GPU core


GPU shader cores without dedicated Neural Accelerators
GPU shader cores with a dedicated Neural Accelerator in every core


First-generation Dynamic Caching
Updated Dynamic Caching


Second-generation hardware-accelerated ray tracing
Hardware-accelerated ray tracing with up to 2x higher gaming performance compared with M4, according to Apple


One 16-core Neural Engine
Two 16-core Neural Engines, totaling 32 cores, which system frameworks can use simultaneously


120GB/s unified memory bandwidth
Up to 170GB/s unified memory bandwidth


SSD storage
SSD storage with PCIe 5.0 support and up to 2x faster read and write performance


Broadcom wireless networking chip
Apple N1 wireless networking chip


Wi-Fi 6E (802.11ax)
Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be)


Bluetooth 5.3
Bluetooth 6



Thread networking technology


Two-port model: Optional Gigabit Ethernet
Four-port model: Gigabit Ethernet as standard
Two-port model: Optional 2.5Gb Ethernet
Four-port model: 2.5Gb Ethernet as standard


Two-port model: One external display up to 6K at 60Hz
Two-port model: One external display up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz


Four-port model: Two external displays up to 6K at 60Hz, or one external display up to 8K at 60Hz
Four-port model: Two external displays up to 6K at 60Hz or 4K at 165Hz, or one external display up to 8K at 60Hz, 5K at 120Hz, or 4K at 240Hz



Four-port model: Support for two external displays over a single Thunderbolt port


100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in multiple printed circuit boards
100% recycled gold plating and tin solder in all Apple-designed printed circuit boards


Over 20% of manufacturing electricity sourced from low-carbon electricity
40% of manufacturing electricity sourced from renewable electricity




Apple claims the following workflow improvements for the M6 ‌iMac‌ compared with the M4 model:


Up to 1.5x faster performance in Microsoft Excel.

Up to 2x faster graphics performance for photo editing in Affinity.

Up to 5x faster prompt processing in LM Studio.

Up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing.



Is It Worth Upgrading From the M4 to M6 iMac?

For most M4 ‌iMac‌ owners, there is little reason to upgrade. The M6's performance improvements are substantial in certain tasks, but casual tasks such as browsing, email, video calls, and streaming are already comfortably within the M4's capabilities. With the same display, camera, speakers, and overall design, the new model is unlikely to meaningfully change how most households use their ‌iMac‌.

Occasional photo editing or gaming can benefit from the M6, but these improvements alone are difficult to justify replacing an otherwise capable computer. The faster networking similarly offers limited incentive unless your current connection is a particular frustration and the rest of your equipment can support the upgrade. For the typical M4 ‌iMac‌ owner, keeping the existing machine is the sensible choice.

Should You Buy the M4 or M6 iMac?

For buyers choosing a new family computer, the M6 ‌iMac‌ is the straightforward choice when comparable configurations are close in price. Its additional performance provides more room for demanding apps and games as your needs change, while retaining the familiar all-in-one experience.

title: Apple’s M6 MacBook Pro is here: Everything you need to know
content:
Macworld





Apple has announced a new 14-inch MacBook Pro powered by M6. This announcement covers the standard-chip model; it does not introduce M6 Pro or M6 Max versions. Preorders begin October 28, with availability from November 6.
The biggest changes center on the processor. M6 moves to a 2-nanometer manufacturing process and increases both CPU and GPU core counts from 10 to 12. It also introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine and higher maximum memory bandwidth.
Wireless connectivity supplies the other major upgrade: Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 replace the M5 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. Apple claims graphics performance improves by up to 30 percent over M5.


FeatureNew 14-inch M6Previous 14-inch M5

Manufacturing process2nmThird-generation 3nm
CPU cores1210
CPU architectureNew complex with super, performance, and efficiency coresEarlier CPU design
GPU cores1210
Graphics performanceUp to 30% faster, Apple claimsComparison baseline
Neural EngineDual 16-core16-core
GPU Neural AcceleratorsRetained across the larger GPUPresent
Maximum memory bandwidthUp to 170GB/s153GB/s
Wi-FiWi-Fi 7Wi-Fi 6E
Bluetooth65.3

 



For more on the redesigned models possibly arriving tomorrow, see our touchscreen MacBook Pro guide.


M6 MacBook Pro release date: When will it launch?
Preorders: October 28, 2026
On sale: November 6
Preorders open Wednesday, October 28, 2026, through Apple’s online store and the Apple Store app. 
Deliveries and sales through Apple Stores and Apple Authorized Resellers begin Friday, November 6, across 35 countries and regions. 
Preorder a M6 MacBook Pro at Apple U.S.
Preorder a M6 MacBook Pro at Apple U.K.


							


M6 MacBook Pro design: What does it look like?

				
					

				
			The M6 MacBook Pro looks just like the previous generation.
John Brandon




As expected, the new model continues the familiar aluminum design in Space Black and Silver. A more ambitious redesign is anticipated for the rumored touchscreen MacBook expected to launch tomorrow.
The M6 MacBook Pro retains the same dimensions and weight as its M5 predecessor. It measures 12.31 inches wide, 8.71 inches deep, and 0.61 inch thick (31.26 × 22.12 × 1.55cm), and weighs 3.4 pounds (1.55kg).
As with the predecessor, its controls include a backlit Magic Keyboard, full-height function keys, Touch ID, and a Force Touch trackpad.


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro display: Resolution and screen quality

				
					

				
			The screen hasn’t changed with the M6 generation.
Foundry




Apple has not announced a screen upgrade in this release. The M6 MacBook Pro continues to feature a Liquid Retina XDR display with an optional nano-texture finish and the same display specifications.
14.2-inch mini-LED Liquid Retina XDR display
3024 × 1964 resolution
ProMotion adaptive refresh rates up to 120Hz
1,600 nits peak HDR brightness
1,000 nits sustained full-screen HDR brightness
Up to 1,000 nits SDR brightness outdoors
P3 wide color and True Tone


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro processor: What does M6 change?
The M6 uses a 2nm manufacturing process, increasing transistor density, and features a 12-core CPU comprising two super cores, four performance cores, and six efficiency cores. That’s up from the M5’s 10-core CPU. Apple’s Mac mini M6 announcement claimed up to 20 percent faster multithreaded performance than M5, although that testing used a Mac mini. Read more about the M6 in our M6 deep dive.
Graphics also get a boost, with a 12-core GPU replacing the M5’s 10-core version. Neural Accelerators and hardware-accelerated ray tracing return, while memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, allowing data to move more quickly between the chip and unified memory.
The M6 introduces a dual 16-core Neural Engine, compared with the M5’s single 16-core engine. For this laptop, Apple reports up to 1.9 times faster Neural Engine performance and 25 percent faster on-device AI workloads versus M5. These are separate measures of performance, with the benefits depending on the task and how an app uses the chip.
The Media Engine retains the M5’s listed capabilities, including hardware acceleration for H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW, alongside AV1 decoding. Dedicated video encoding and decoding hardware helps handle demanding media tasks efficiently, but Apple’s comparison sheet lists no new codec support for M6.


						

							






SpecsM6M5

CPU12 cores: 2 super, 4 performance, 6 efficiency10 cores: 4 super, 6 efficiency
GPU12 cores10 cores
Neural EngineDual 16-coreSingle 16-core
Memory bandwidthUp to 170GB/s153GB/s

 






M6 MacBook Pro RAM: How much memory does it have?
The M6 MacBook Pro starts with 16GB of unified memory, with 24GB and 32GB configurations also available – the same capacities offered with M5. However, memory bandwidth increases from 153GB/s to up to 170GB/s, helping the chip access data more quickly.
Additional unified memory gives applications and graphics workloads more room to operate simultaneously. For local AI, capacity affects which models fit in memory, while bandwidth affects how quickly data can move.
Buying advice: Choose 16GB for everyday productivity; consider 24GB for heavier multitasking and creative work, or 32GB for memory-intensive projects and local AI experimentation.


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro Connectivity: What ports and wireless options are there?
Wireless connectivity improves with Wi-Fi 7 (802.11be) and Bluetooth 6, replacing the M5 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3. Wi-Fi 7 availability varies by country.
The physical connections remain unchanged, including three Thunderbolt 4 (USB-C) ports, HDMI, an SDXC card slot, and a 3.5mm headphone jack with support for high-impedance headphones.


						

							


M6 MacBook Pro battery, MagSafe, and charging
Apple rates the M6 MacBook Pro for up to 24 hours of video streaming or 16 hours of wireless web browsing, matching the M5 model. These are Apple’s test figures; we’ll be running our own independent battery tests to establish whether M6 delivers better endurance during everyday work or more demanding tasks.
In the U.S. a 70W USB-C power adapter ships with both models, this is an extra expense in the U.K. and Europe (as was the case for the M5 model). Fast charging requires a 96W or higher USB Power Delivery source, so buyers who want that capability should check their adapter’s output. The listed 70W adapter does not meet Apple’s fast-charging requirement.


						

							






Battery/charging specificationBoth models

Wireless web browsingUp to 16 hours
Video streamingUp to 24 hours
Battery capacity72.4Wh lithium-polymer
Power adapter listed70W USB-C
Fast chargingRequires a 96W or higher USB PD power source

 






M6 MacBook Pro: Price
$1,999/£1,999 starting price
The U.S. and U.K.  starting price is $1,999/£1,999, or $1,899/£1,899 for eligible education buyers. That matches the outgoing model’s current U.S. starting price, rather than its original launch price. 


						

							






Model and pricing pointU.S. starting priceU.K. starting price

M5 at October 2025 launch$1,599£1,599
Outgoing M5, current listing$1,999£1,999
New M6$1,999£1,999
M6 vs. current M5No increaseAwait confirmation
M6 vs. original M5 U.S. launch$400 more$400 more

 






Should you buy the M6 MacBook Pro?
Buy if: You need a replacement now and the standard MacBook Pro meets your workload. Buyers moving from older machines are more likely to notice the improvement than recent M5 owners.
Don’t buy if: Your M5 already handles your work comfortably. Wait for independent benchmarks before paying to replace it, especially if one particular application drives your decision.
Which configuration? Prioritize memory around the projects you actually run. For demanding graphics, large datasets, or professional video work, compare the full specifications and benchmarks of Pro and Max models rather than choosing solely by the newer “M6” name.
Wait if: An OLED touchscreen or redesigned chassis would materially affect your purchase. These may arrive tomorrow, and for a more powerful chip, reports indicate the M7 Pro/Max is expected in 2027, rather than an M5 Pro and M5 Max now.


						

							




Of the five generations of MacBook Pro, five have been released in the October/November timeframe. The list below also demonstrates that Apple doesn’t always introduce the standard, Pro and Max versions of a chip generation together.  
M5 Pro & M5 Max MacBook Pro: March 2026
M5 MacBook Pro: October 2025
M4, M4 Pro & M4 Max MacBook Pro: November 2024
M3, M3 Pro & M3 Max MacBook Pro: November 2023
M2 Pro & M2 Max MacBook Pro: January 2023
M2 MacBook Pro: June 2022
M1 Pro & M1 Max MacBook Pro: October 2021
M1 MacBook Pro: November 2020

title: Apple’s M6 MacBook Pro isn’t very ‘exciting’ at all
content:
Macworld





The new MacBook Pro has arrived, but if you don’t have access to a benchmarking app, you’d be hard-pressed to know you were using one. As expected, Apple rolled out the M6 update to its entry-level MacBook Pro, but there isn’t anything obviously new. The colors are the same (silver and space black). The memory and storage options are the same. The display is the same. And thankfully, the price is the same.
The M6 MacBook Pro is, quite literally, a chip-and-ship update. The new M6 chip, which Apple already unveiled in the Mac mini in late August, is a relatively minor refresh of the M5, which delivered a nice graphics boost. Sure it’s faster, but you’ll need to see benchmark numbers to see the difference. Here are the specs:
M6 chip
12-core CPU (2 super, 4 performance, and 6 efficiency) 
12-core GPU
Neural Accelerators
Hardware-accelerated ray tracing
Dual 16-core Neural Engine 
Up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth
Media engine
Hardware-accelerated H.264, HEVC, ProRes, and ProRes RAW
Video decode engine
Video encode engine
ProRes encode and decode engine
AV1 decode
That’s identical to the chip we got in the Mac mini, so no surprises there. The M5 MacBook Pro was the last of Apple’s laptops to still run Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3, so it also got an upgrade to Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 with the N1 chip. But if you don’t have a Wi-Fi 7 router and a very fast network, you’re not going to notice that either.
From what we’re hearing, this MacBook Pro will be the last of its kind. Apple is expected to release a touchscreen MacBook Pro with a new design this week. That new design will reportedly make its way to the non-touchscreen models with next year’s M7 update, so if you have an M4 or M5, you can probably sit this one out.
The M6 MacBook Pro is part of a week of “exciting” releases that has also included the A20 Pro iPad mini and M6 iMac. But the main event will be Wednesday, when Apple releases its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro. You can pre-order the M6 MacBook Pro tomorrow starting at 10:10 a.m. PT for delivery next Friday, November 6. It starts at the same $1,999 with 16GB of RAM and 1TB of storage, which is a small victory in this age of price hikes.

title: iMac gains M6 chip and performance boost, but little else changes
content:
Macworld





Apple today announced an M6 update to its iMac desktop line, heralding “a major boost in performance and AI capabilities.” But other than the upgrade from an M4 to an M6 chip there’s little change from the previous model.
Admittedly that chip upgrade, leaping two generations in a single refresh, is a significant one. Apple claims the M6 will deliver up to 1.5x faster performance than M4 in apps such as Excel, up to 2x faster graphics performance, and up to 2x higher gaming performance with ray tracing. AI, inevitably, is foregrounded too, with Apple claiming the M6 is capable of up to 5x faster on-device AI prompt processing in LM Studio. This could be a worthwhile upgrade if performance in these categories is a bottleneck for you.
There are also some connectivity improvements. Wi-Fi has been bumped from version 6E (802.11ax) to 7 (802.11be), and Bluetooth from 5.3 to 6. Gigabit Ethernet on the M4 model has been upgraded to 2.5Gb Ethernet here. And Apple claims the new iMac offers up to 2x faster SSD read and write, which means “apps launch quickly, and large files like photo libraries and video projects load in an instant.” Macworld will put all this to the test when we get hold of a review sample, of course, but we’ve seen what Apple’s done with SSD speeds this year and are inclined to believe the claims.

				
					

				
			
The new iMac has an M6 chip and little else that’s new.

Apple




Beyond that, however, there’s not much to say. The opening section of the press release promises “blazing-fast performance, enhanced connectivity, Siri AI, and macOS 27, all in a stunning design in seven vibrant colors.” The first two I’ve already discussed. And the rest–Siri AI, macOS 27, the attractive design, and the seven colors–are available on the previous models. It’s not a good sign when a company has to fall back on old features that early in a new product’s announcement.
As far as we can tell the M6 iMac is physically identical to the M4 model. It has the same dimensions and comes in the same colors. Its screen is the same size and has the same specs. Even the camera and speaker setups are unchanged, and you get the same number of ports: either two or four USB 4, depending on which model you pick, plus a 3.5mm headphone jack.
We loved the iMac M4, which our reviewer said “might be the best iMac ever.” And there’s a lot to like about the M6 chip refresh. So this is unlikely to be a bad product. It’s just not very different from the last one. And the best part might be that there isn’t another price hike. You can pre-order the new iMac beginning tomorrow at 10:10 a.m. PT, with deliveries beginning next Friday.
For exhaustive details of and expert reaction to all the Apple products getting unveiled this week, check out our ongoing live blog. Most of them are more interesting than this one.

title: M6 MacBook Pro's 170GB/s Memory Bandwidth Skips Base 16GB Model

title: Apple Updates Creator Studio With New Tools and AI Features
content:
Apple today announced a new update to its Creator Studio suite of apps, adding a number of additional features and tools across Mac, iPad, and iPhone. 


Amongst the new features, Final Cut Pro for Mac now includes built-in MotionVFX, which was previously a third-party content maker. The integration brings over thousands of effects, plug-ins, transitions, templates, titles and motion graphics tools, including rotoscoping, tracking, and color grading. Apple's curated Content Hub now also includes video assets and is available in Final Cut Pro.

Pixelmator Pro's Generate Fill now lets users select an area of an image and describe the change they want in natural language, while Logic Pro adds an intelligent assistant in beta, a redesigned sound Browser, and an enhanced Stem Splitter that can now isolate drum parts without the original multitracks. 

Keynote, Pages, and Numbers are all gaining assistants that understand document context, plus there's Model Context Protocol support which lets external AI agents read, edit, and automate actions in the apps. 

The Logic Pro assistant is Mac-only, and requires macOS 27 on an Apple Intelligence-capable Mac, whereas the Keynote, Pages, and Numbers assistants require an Apple Intelligence-capable device running iOS 27, iPadOS 27, or macOS 27. MCP support is Mac-only as well, requiring macOS 27. All of the assistants are in beta and available in U.S. English only.

title: Apple Announces New 14-Inch MacBook Pro With M6 Chip
content:
Apple today announced a refreshed 14-inch MacBook Pro featuring the M6 chip, upgraded connectivity specifications, and more.



The M6 chip in the ‌MacBook Pro‌ features a 12-core CPU with 2 super cores, 4 performance cores, and 6 efficiency cores, paired with a 12-core GPU. This is up from the M5 chip with a 10-core CPU with 4 super cores and 6 efficiency cores, paired with a 10-core GPU.

M6 features an advanced 12-core CPU with the world's fastest CPU core, so everything from productivity tasks to more demanding pro workflows feels incredibly fast and responsive. The 12-core GPU delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads when compared to M5, making the 14-inch MacBook Pro with M6 a compelling value for users who need serious power.


The Neural Engine doubles from 16-cores to a dual 16-core Neural Engine system with 32 total cores. Memory bandwidth also increases from 153GB/s to 170GB/s, but only on models with 24GB and 32GB of memory.

With additional Neural Accelerators in the GPU and a Dual 16-core Neural Engine, M6 turns MacBook Pro into an even more powerful platform for AI — from taking advantage of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence features across apps and macOS to running LLMs locally, all while preserving user privacy.


Alongside the M6 chip, the new 14-inch ‌MacBook Pro‌ now features support for Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 connectivity via Apple's N1 wireless chip. It can also now drive dual external 4K displays at up to 165Hz, up from 144Hz.

title: Apple Announces New iMac With M6 Chip and More
content:
Apple today announced a new 24-inch iMac with the M6 chip for faster performance, an N1 chip with Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support, faster SSD speeds, and more.


The new iMac has the same design as the previous model with the M4 chip, and the color options remain the same: blue, green, pink, yellow, purple, orange, and silver. The all-in-one desktop computer still has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display with up to 500 nits brightness, and a 12-megapixel Center Stage camera with Desk View support.

All models continue to have six speakers, three microphones, a 3.5mm headphone jack, and support for Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.

in the Mac mini in August, the M6 chip features the first-ever dual Neural Engine with two 16-core engines, up from one in previous chips. For graphics, the iMac now has Neural Accelerators in each GPU core for the first time. The M6 chip also has up to 170GB/s memory bandwidth, up from 120GB/s for the M4 chip.

Geekbench results for the M6 chip already surfaced for the Mac mini, so we know that the new higher-end iMac should offer up to around 40% faster CPU performance compared to the previous model with the M4 chip. Apple says the new model is up to 12× faster than the model with the M1 chip, and up to 18× faster than the final Intel-based iMac. 

Apple also says the new iMac has up to 2× faster graphics and up to 5× faster on-device AI performance compared to the previous model.


In the U.S., pricing starts at $1,499 for a lower-end configuration powered by the M6 chip with a 10-core CPU, a 10-core GPU, a dual 16-core Neural Engine, 16GB of RAM, 256GB of storage, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. The equivalent previous model also started at $1,499 after receiving a price increase in June — it was originally $1,299.

A higher-end configuration for $1,699 bumps the M6 chip up to a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU and has four Thunderbolt 4 ports instead of two.

The maximum storage capacity available is 2TB, while RAM tops out at 32GB.

A power adapter with a faster 2.5 Gigabit Ethernet port is a $30 upgrade option for the base model and comes standard on the higher-end model. The previous iMac's power adapter has a Gigabit Ethernet port, aka 1 Gigabit.

With the Apple-designed N1 chip, the iMac now supports faster Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6, up from Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3 for the previous model.

The jump from the M4 chip to the M6 chip results in the new iMac having up to twice as fast SSD read and write speeds, thanks to PCIe 5.0 support.

The new iMac will be available to pre-order starting Wednesday, October 28 at 10:10 a.m. Pacific Time, and it is set to launch on Friday, November 6.

title: These iOS 27.2 features will make you want to download the latest updates right away
content:
Macworld





After weeks of development with enrolled beta testers, iOS 27.2 is available to all iPhone users as a stable release, along with macOS, iPadOS, watchOS, and tvOS. The first major update to iOS 27 introduces several handy enhancements to Siri AI, along with some major additions to Apple TV and HomePod.
What happened to iOS 27.1?
It’s odd for Apple to jump from iOS 27.0.1 to iOS 27.2, but there’s a simple explanation: iOS 27.1 was strictly for the iPhone Duo. There was never a developer or public beta release, but Apple likely had a similar program for the software in-house as to not leak specific features for the folding phone. In fact, iPhone Duo users had to update to a newer build of iOS 27.1 after unboxing their phones. 
iOS 27.2 is compatible with all iPhones, including the Duo, so iOS 27.1 might go down as the shortest-lived update Apple has ever released.
Siri AI expansion
Siri AI first launched with iOS 27.0, unlocking a comprehensive chatbot experience in a dedicated app—plus the ability to recall personal data and take in-app action. The initial version, however, was limited to a single language. While the assistant could comprehend many languages when texting it, its main interface and voice commands only supported English. With iOS 27.2, Siri AI officially expands language support to include French, Spanish, Portuguese, Japanese, and Korean.
The latest update also expands what Siri AI can do in Apple’s native communication apps. In Messages, Siri now suggests relevant actions under individual texts when needed. For example, if someone mentions a date, the assistant will surface a shortcut to quickly add it to the Calendar app. Meanwhile, the Phone app’s Call Context feature now highlights saved anniversaries, a welcome addition to the existing birthday reminders.
Another new feature is Siri’s ability to reference previous queries. Siri will now be able to access prior chats even when not continuing a conversation in the Siri app.
iOS 27.2 should also expand Siri AI’s platform availability, unlocking it on the second-generation Apple TV 4K and newer models. Once you install the latest iOS and tvOS builds, your Apple TV 4K will rely on your nearby iPhone to handle personal requests on the big screen. It’s worth noting, however, that Siri AI has yet to be activated on the tvOS 27.2 Release Candidate at the time of writing, and since the new Apple TV doesn’t release until November 13, it may require a separate update.

				
					

				
			
Siri can now suggest relevant actions in Messages.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Apple TV profiles
Speaking of Apple TV, iOS 27.2 brings a highly requested feature to the streaming service. Similar to Netflix, the TV app on your iPhone now allows you to create multiple viewer profiles tied to a single Apple Account.
If you tend to share your personal iPhone or iPad with a family member, they will be able to use your subscription to watch original movies and series without altering your queue or watch history. This does not impact the existing Family Sharing perk that allows up to six independent Apple Accounts to take advantage of a single subscription on their own devices.
Some of the features supported by Apple TV profiles include picking a name and avatar, restricting adult content, adding a 4-digit PIN, and setting autoplay defaults. Notably, the primary account holder will be able to view, manage, and delete any of the secondary profiles created using their account.
Sound Glow on HomePods
The latest OS update revitalizes all HomePod models except the original full-size model from 2018. Once you install iOS and HomePod Software 27.2, you’ll be able to toggle a new Sound Glow setting in the iPhone’s built-in Home app. 
The feature distills a playing song’s album art into a color blob that animates on the HomePod’s top display in sync with the rhythm. While Sound Glow doesn’t affect the actual audio, it does make vibing to music more fun—especially in pitch-black environments, which amplify the dramatic effect.
Other handy HomePod options in the OS 27.2 release include a Lock Controls toggle that disables the touchscreen. If your smart speaker suffers from ghost touch issues, you’ll be able to make it usable again by turning off touch input. 

				
					

				
			
HomePod mini gets a new Sound Glow feature in iOS 27.2.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




App Switcher on watchOS
After updating your iPhone, you’ll want to install watchOS 27.2 on your Apple Watch. This release brings back the App Switcher on watchOS after version 27.0 removed it, making it possible to force-quit misbehaving apps again.
It’s not as simple as before, however. Instead of double-clicking the Digital Crown, you’ll now have to tap and hold on the bottom of the screen inside an app to reveal the App Switcher. The retired mechanism will be reassigned to the Apple Watch Series 12’s Live Rewind feature when it debuts later this year.

				
					

				
			
You can now easily quit stubborn apps on Apple Watch after installing watchOS 27.2.

Mahmoud Itani/Foundry




Apple Pencil support for iPhone Duo
Even though the iPhone Duo only just hit stores a couple of days ago, there’s already an update and it’s a pretty big one. You can now use your Apple Pencil on either Duo screen and attach it to the side like the iPad. However, only the USB-C Apple Pencil works with the Duo, so you miss out on a few Apple Pencil Pro features, including pressure sensitivity and double-tap/squeeze gestures. 
Where’s the new Health app?
If you’ve been following Apple news, you may have read about the revamped Health app that surfaced during the iOS 27.2 beta cycle. While it has been removed from iOS 27.2’s final build, the overhauled app appears to still be on track to arrive later this year, as Apple originally promised. It will most likely reappear in iOS 27.3, due to launch in December.
Even if you don’t heavily use Siri AI, Apple TV, or HomePod, we advise you to install iOS 27.2 to apply the bug fixes and security patches (over 150 in iOS alone) included with this release. To get started, go to the Settings app on an iPhone 11 or later, followed by General, then Software Update. Hit the Update button and keep your iPhone connected to a power source until the installation completes.

title: How to keep politicians from flooding your iPhone with campaign texts
content:
Political campaign texts are relentless ahead of Election Day, with fundraising appeals piling up in Messages. One iPhone setting can silence their alerts without forcing you to block each unfamiliar number.

Political texts plague everyone
Blocking a number doesn't help much when the next fundraising appeal arrives from a different one. Political fundraising groups even raised objections when Apple expanded message filtering in iOS 26, concerned that donation requests would go unnoticed.
Apple's Screen Unknown Senders feature separates messages based on whether you've established contact with the sender, not whether a message looks like spam. It moves texts from unfamiliar numbers into a separate folder and generally silences their notifications without preventing delivery.
The feature was off by default in iOS 26 unless you'd previously enabled the older Filter Unknown Senders setting. That means even an updated iPhone might still be letting every campaign appeal into your main conversation list.

title: iOS 27.2 Features: Everything New in iOS 27.2
content:
Apple released iOS 27.2, uniting the iPhone Duo and other iPhone models on the same version of iOS. iOS 27.2 is the first major iOS 27 update, and it adds several useful new features.


Siri AI Improvements

Siri AI can recall past conversations you had with it, so you can ask ‌Siri‌ about something it told you before, like a restaurant it previously recommended. It's also able to draw on more sources:

 	
Photos attached to Messages

 	
Calendar event attendees

 	
Voicemails


Apple says you'll also get better results from Safari history and Reading List.

There's a redesigned Excluded Apps feature that lets you quickly select which apps ‌Siri‌, Search, and suggestions can access. The prior App Access feature required excluding apps individually.

There's also granular text selection, so you can select and copy just the part of a ‌Siri‌ response you need.

‌Siri‌ AI requires an iPhone 15 Pro or later.

Siri AI Languages

‌Siri‌ AI is now available in more languages, including French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, and Spanish. ‌Siri‌ AI is still not available in the EU or mainland China.

Messages

Suggestions in Messages have been added in iOS 27.2. The feature was available during the ‌iOS 27‌ beta testing period, but was removed before launch.


Messages suggestions show tappable shortcuts in a conversation based on context, so you can do things like track a package with a tap, or add a dinner invite to the Calendar app.

You can choose the suggestions you want, with options to add Calendar, Reminders, Notes, Maps, and Flights and Packages.
Apple Music

iOS 27.2 introduces a new Apple Music icon that goes with Apple's recent ‌Apple Music‌ rebranding. The icon is black and white, replacing the red icon. Apple also changed the color of the highlights in the navigation bar and other areas of the ‌Apple Music‌ app to remove the red color.


Photos

Shared Albums in the ‌Photos‌ app now have an edit option for captions and comments. Apple also added a feature for avoiding duplicate photos, and there's now a reminder before albums expire so users can save important photos and videos.

SynthID

iOS 27.2 includes SynthID labeling for Image Playground images and some ‌Photos‌ app edits. Watermarks are added when using Extend and Reframe in ‌Photos‌, and for large edits with the Clean Up tool. You can check images for SynthID using Google's SynthID Detector website.



Podcasts

The Home tab in the Podcasts app has separate sections for New Episodes and Continue Playing. The new sections replace Up Next.



Games

The Friends tab in the Games app now includes context on friend suggestions and shows recent games played on friends' player pages.

Apple TV

Apple TV app users can now create profiles in the account settings section on the iPhone and iPad. Profiles only require a name, profile rating, and information about whether the user is a child.



Creating a profile for a child limits content to a PG rating by default, but there is a customize option for finer control. Users can select age ratings for TV shows and movies that are appropriate for the child based on their age.

Phone

The Call Context feature in the Phone app reminds you of a contact's anniversary when you call them, as long as you've saved the date in the Contacts app.



FaceTime

FaceTime Dual Capture is now available in group ‌FaceTime‌ calls. Dual Capture is a feature that lets you stream ‌FaceTime‌ video content from the front and rear cameras at the same time. On a compatible device running ‌iOS 27‌, flipping the camera while on a ‌FaceTime‌ call automatically turns on Dual Capture.

iPhone 17, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro, ‌iPhone 17‌ Pro Max, iPhone Air, iPhone 18 Pro, ‌iPhone 18 Pro‌ Max, and ‌iPhone Duo‌.

Apple also added an option to add a third-party sign language interpreter or live captioner to a call.

Shortcuts

‌iOS 27‌ includes new automations, actions, and improvements for the Shortcuts app. There's a new "when my iPhone is opened or closed" automation for the ‌iPhone Duo‌.

An updated Workout automation adds support for the Fitness app, and the App automation can provide the name of the app that was closed.

Window layout can be configured with the "Show Actions" and Show Describe a Shortcut" menu items, and Shortcut names and icons can be edited from the library.

iPhone Duo Updates

iOS 27.2 adds Apple Pencil USB-C support to the ‌iPhone Duo‌. It also includes Edge Light to illuminate your face during video calls.



Multiview

iOS 27.2 expands Multiview in the ‌Apple TV‌ app to the iPhone, so users can watch up to four live sports streams simultaneously.

Multiview works for sports events included in an ‌Apple TV‌ subscription: Major League Soccer (MLS), Formula 1 (F1) in the U.S., and Friday Night Baseball doubleheaders during the Major League Baseball season.

Clock App

There are smaller a.m. and p.m. labels in the alarm list in the Clock app.



EU - App Tracking Transparency

App Tracking Transparency supports an alternative expanded prompt for EU users along with re-prompting on an annual basis. The alternative prompt is required for users in France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Romania.

Health App

Apple tested its redesigned Health app in the iOS 27.2 beta, but it won't be coming out until later this year and is not included in iOS 27.2.

Security Fixes

iOS 27.2 addresses more than 160 security vulnerabilities. None of the vulnerabilities were actively exploited, but it's always a good idea to update when this many fixes are included.

title: Why Can't iPhone Duo Users Make Eye Contact on FaceTime?
content:
FaceTime's Eye Contact setting is missing on the iPhone Duo, MacRumors can confirm. The setting was first flagged as absent by MacRumors forum member TwoBytes, who noticed their eyes looking "a little off" during a call. 


Introduced in iOS 14, Eye Contact uses machine learning to subtly adjust your eyes during a video call to make it seem like you're looking into the camera lens, even though you're actually looking at the image of the other person on your screen. 

While it may seem the obvious cause, the iPhone Duo's lack of Face ID and TrueDepth camera is unlikely to be the reason for Eye Contact's absence, since iPhone SE models with Touch ID also include the option in Settings. One possibility is the position of the inner display's under-display camera, which sits toward the right-hand side of the screen, away from the center where the other caller's face usually appears.

Correcting for that larger, sideways offset is going to be different than for the small vertical gap on a regular iPhone.

when the Duo is fully open.

We've reached out to Apple for a technical explanation about the lack of Eye Contact on the iPhone Duo.

jailbroke the iPhone Duo on launch day and demonstrated an untethered iOS 27.0.1 jailbreak. Calif researcher Stefan Esser recently said that "most" of the vulnerabilities used for its jailbreak are fixed in iOS 27.2.

title: iPhone AI Images and Edits Now Have a Hidden Watermark
content:
Images generated with Image Playground and some photos edited with Apple Intelligence will now include a SynthID watermark. Apple announced plans to add SynthID support back in June, and the feature is live in iOS 27.2.


SynthID is a Google-created tool that identifies AI-generated content. It watermarks images and videos at the pixel level instead of adding metadata. Google says it does not affect image quality and is meant to survive cropping, filters, and compression. SynthID is used by Google, Apple, OpenAI, and others.

SynthID Detector website.

Photos app tools, images altered with Extend and Reframe had SynthID watermarks when checked, but Clean Up watermarking seemed to depend on the size of the edit. With small edits, no watermark was added. Larger Clean Up edits included a SynthID watermark.
